hints: Every value is between 1 and m, and neighbors may differ by at most one.
Let dp[v] count valid prefixes ending with value v.
At each position, a fixed input value permits only that value; zero permits all values.
analogy: Extend each partial array by a value matching the next clue and close to its last value.
example: For description [2,0,2], the middle can be 1, 2, or 3, giving three arrays.
algorithm: Initialize first-position counts according to its known value or all possibilities. For each next position, dpNew[v]=dp[v-1]+dp[v]+dp[v+1] if allowed by the clue, modulo the modulus; sum final states.
correctness: A valid prefix ending at v can be extended exactly from previous endings v-1, v, or v+1; the clue filter enforces known positions.
